title: Managed databases vs databases on EC2

kcs.statement: With a managed database such as RDS, AWS handles provisioning, OS and engine patching, automated backups and hardware failure, while the customer manages schemas, data, user access and network settings.
Run a database on EC2 only when you need OS-level access, an engine or version the managed services do not offer, or full configuration control; you then own patching, backups and high availability.

problem_ideas: Sort tasks for RDS: OS patching, creating database users, encrypting data, replacing failed disks, choosing the security group
A vendor app needs a custom plug-in installed on the database host OS: RDS or EC2?
A team of two developers has no DBA: which option reduces operations work?
Same tasks for a self-managed MySQL on EC2: who now patches the engine?
A legacy engine version is no longer offered by RDS: what are the options?
Estimate which costs disappear when moving from EC2-hosted to managed: licences, admin hours, backup scripts
